plain.text: Paul went to Corinth. There he met Aquila and his wife Priscilla, Jews who had recently left Italy because Emperor Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome. They were tentmakers, like Paul, so he stayed and worked with them. Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue. When Silas and Timothy arrived, Paul devoted himself fully to preaching that Jesus was the Messiah. When some opposed him, he moved next door to the house of Titius Justus. Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed, and many Corinthians believed and were baptised. One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: "Do not be afraid; keep on speaking. For I am with you, and no one will attack and harm you, because I have many people in this city." Paul stayed a year and a half, teaching God's word.

When Gallio was governor of Achaia, some Jews brought Paul to court, accusing him of persuading people to worship God against the law. Gallio said that if this were a matter of wrongdoing he would hear it, but since it was about words, names and their own law, they should settle it themselves. He drove them from the court. The crowd then beat Sosthenes, the synagogue leader, in front of the court, but Gallio showed no concern.

Paul stayed in Corinth for some time, then sailed for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila. At Ephesus he reasoned in the synagogue. They asked him to stay longer, but he declined, promising to return if it was God's will. He landed at Caesarea, greeted the church in Jerusalem, and went down to Antioch.

After some time in Antioch, Paul travelled through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples. Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a learned man with a thorough knowledge of the Scriptures, came to Ephesus. He spoke with great fervour and taught about Jesus accurately, though he knew only the baptism of John. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they invited him to their home and explained the way of God more adequately. Apollos went to Achaia, where he was a great help to the believers, vigorously showing from the Scriptures that Jesus was the Messiah.

summary.bigIdea: In Corinth and beyond, Paul and his co-workers, including Priscilla and Aquila, keep spreading and strengthening the faith.
points: Paul works as a tentmaker with Priscilla and Aquila while preaching.
The Lord tells Paul, "Do not be afraid; keep on speaking... I am with you."
Priscilla and Aquila gently help Apollos understand the way of God more fully.
summary.reflection: Priscilla and Aquila taught Apollos privately and kindly. How could you encourage someone's faith in a gentle way?
